hub_subtitle: Business English para seguros, reuniões e entrevistas — e o desbloqueio da fala, do primeiro dia ao último

lesson.menu_title: What Will Happen? -- Will for Promises, Predictions and Decisions on the Spot
lesson.menu_desc: A aula em que o inglês da Paula deixa de ser sobre o que ela já viveu e passa a ser sobre o que ela vai fazer. Nas aulas 14 e 15 ela contou o passado; na 13 ela aprendeu o going to dos planos já decididos. Hoje entra a outra metade do futuro: will — a palavra da promessa (I will send it today), da previsão (the meeting will probably be long) e da decisão tomada na hora de falar (don't worry, I'll check now). E é esta última que resolve o maior medo dela: quando alguém pergunta algo que ela não sabe, ela não precisa mais pedir desculpa — ela promete. I will check and I will call you back. A aula é de LEITURA: ela lê o comunicado da Sofia com o ano inteiro da equipe — o sistema novo em março, os clientes novos em junho e, em novembro, a reunião anual em Miami, a primeira viagem internacional dela pela Zurich. Seis palavras novas (promise, probably, maybe, confirm, delay, worry), o Greg prometendo buscar ela no aeroporto, e a Sofia fechando com a frase que a aula inteira constrói: “por dois anos você foi uma voz numa call; em novembro você vai estar na sala.” -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 16 -- What Will Happen?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Paula Morales | Lesson 16 -- What Will Happen? (Will)
lesson.grammar_point: future with will -- promises (I will send it today), predictions (it will probably be long) and decisions made at the moment of speaking (I'll check now); will + bare verb for every person, contraction 'll and negative won't, contrasted with going to for plans already decided

listenings.text: Hi, Paula. David here. In November you will come to Miami, and I want to tell you what will happen there, because nobody ever tells you these things. You will land, and the first thing you will feel is the heat. Then you will come to the office, and about forty people will say hello to you in one hour. You will not remember all the names. Nobody does. I promise you, that is normal. On the first morning we will start at nine, and the meeting will probably finish late, because it always does. At some point somebody will ask a question about a large risk in Brazil, and you will know the answer better than anyone in that room. Now here is the part I really want to say. Ten years ago I went to my first international meeting, and I was so nervous that I decided one thing before I walked in. I will not speak today. I will only listen. And I did not speak. Not one word, in three days. It was the biggest mistake of that year. So this time, no. Say one thing on the first day. Just one. It does not have to be perfect, and it will not be perfect. Say it anyway. See you in November, Paula.

Good morning, Paula. Sofia here. I want to say something about the small word you learned today, because I think you will need it more than you know. Will is not only grammar. Will is what you say when somebody asks you for something and you do not have the answer yet. I will check, and I will call you back. That sentence saved my career, and I am serious. When I started, I thought a professional was a person who knew everything immediately. That is not true. A professional is a person who promises something and then does it. Now, about November. I told the team you will come to Miami, and one person asked me, will she be ready? And I said yes, she will. Not because your English will be perfect in November, because it will not be, and that is fine. You will be ready because you will say the three sentences that matter. I will check. I will send it today. I promise. Paula, for two years you were a voice on a call. In November you will be in the room, and the people who only heard you will finally see you. So this week, practice one thing for me. Every time you do not know something, do not stop, and do not apologize. Say, I will find out, and I will come back to you. Say it until it is automatic. See you Thursday, Paula.

reading.rtitle: The Year Ahead — A Message to the Large Risks Team
paras: This year will be different for our team. In March the new system will arrive, and everyone will learn it together. It will probably take two months, so don't worry: nobody will be alone with it. I will book the training days myself.

In June we will receive the new large-risk clients from the north. Paula will take the international accounts, and she will speak with Miami every week. Maybe the first calls will be difficult. That is normal, and it will not stay difficult.

In November we will all meet in Miami for the annual meeting. Three days. Paula, this will be your first trip with us, and I promise you one thing: you will not be a voice on a call. You will be in the room.

I will confirm the dates in September, and I will send the hotel and the flights in October. If there is a delay with a visa, tell me early and we will solve it together. This year will ask a lot of us. I think we will be ready.
reading.source: Sofia — Zurich, Large Risks — message to the team

reading.prompt: What is the main idea of Sofia's message?
choices: It is a list of the policies the team sold last year, with the final numbers.
It is Sofia's plan for the year: a new system in March, new clients in June, and the Miami meeting in November — with a promise to Paula that she will be in the room, not a voice on a call.
It is an invitation to a holiday in Miami, with no work and no meetings.

items: The new system will arrive in June.
f
No. The system will arrive in March. June is when the new large-risk clients from the north will come.
Sofia says the team will learn the new system together.
t
Yes: "everyone will learn it together... nobody will be alone with it." She will even book the training days herself.
Paula will speak with Miami every week.
t
Yes: "Paula will take the international accounts, and she will speak with Miami every week."
The meeting in Miami will be in September.
f
No. The meeting will be in November. September is when Sofia will confirm the dates; October is when she will send the hotel and the flights.
Sofia promises Paula that she will only be a voice on a call.
f
The opposite, and it is the heart of the message: "you will not be a voice on a call. You will be in the room."

bank.label: Promises and decisions on the spot / Promessas e decisões na hora
items: I will check and I will call you back.
I will send it today, I promise.
Don't worry — I'll do it now.
I will confirm the dates tomorrow.
I won't forget.

bank.label: Predictions / Previsões
items: The meeting will probably be long.
Maybe the flight will have a delay.
I think it will be fine.
It will probably take two months.
It won't be easy, but we will be ready.

items.situation: A client asks for a number you don't have right now. Answer with a promise, not an apology.
tips: I don't have it now. I will check and I will call you back.
I'll find out today and I'll come back to you.

items.situation: Greg asks what time your flight will land in Miami. You are not sure yet.
tips: I'm not sure yet. I will confirm the flight next week.
Maybe it will land in the morning. I'll send you the number.

items.situation: A colleague is worried about the new system. Say it will not be hard, and offer help on the spot.
tips: Don't worry. I'll help you with it.
It won't be difficult. I'll show you tomorrow.

items.situation: Make a prediction about the Miami meeting. Use 'probably'.
tips: The meeting will probably be long.

items.situation: Sofia asks if you will send the report today. Promise it.
tips: Yes, I will send it today. I promise.
I'll send it before six, I promise.

items.situation: Your flight has a delay of three hours. Call Greg and tell him what you will do.
tips: There is a delay, so I will arrive late. I'll call you when I land.
My flight has a delay of three hours. Don't worry, I'll send you a message.
